_meta.indication: Treatment of adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic urothelial cancer who have previously received a PD-1 or PD-L1 inhibitor and a platinum-containing chemotherapy in the neoadjuvant/adjuvant, locally advanced or metastatic setting; approved under accelerated approval based on tumor response rate.

pivotal_trials.design: Single-arm, open-label, multicenter trial of enfortumab vedotin 1.25 mg/kg monotherapy.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with locally advanced or metastatic urothelial cancer who previously received a platinum-based combination regimen and a PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Confirmed objective response rate (ORR) per RECIST v1.1 by blinded independent central review (BICR); secondary: duration of response (DOR).
pivotal_trials.result: Confirmed ORR 44% (55/125; 95% CI 35.1, 53.2), with CR 12% and PR 32%; median duration of response 7.6 months (95% CI 6.3, NE).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥20%): fatigue, peripheral neuropathy, decreased appetite, rash, alopecia, nausea, dysgeusia, diarrhea, dry eye, pruritus and dry skin. Most common Grade ≥3 reactions (≥5%): rash, diarrhea, and fatigue. Peripheral neuropathy occurred in 49% of 310 patients (2% Grade 3). Discontinuation due to adverse reactions occurred in 16%, most commonly peripheral neuropathy (6%).
target_moa: Nectin-4-directed antibody-drug conjugate: a human IgG1 antibody against Nectin-4 (a cell-surface adhesion protein) conjugated to MMAE, a microtubule-disrupting agent, via a protease-cleavable linker.
companion_dx_detail: No companion diagnostic was submitted; Nectin-4 expression was not a criterion for enrollment in EV-201.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was held; the benefit-risk profile was considered clearly favorable with no controversial issues.

description.text: Added new indication for Padcev in combination with pembrolizumab as neoadjuvant and adjuvant treatment for adults with muscle invasive bladder cancer ineligible for cisplatin-containing chemotherapy

summary.text: PADCEV received accelerated approval under 21 CFR Part 601 Subpart E based on the surrogate endpoint of confirmed ORR from single-arm Phase 2 study EV-201. It was a breakthrough-therapy designated ADC and was granted priority review. Continued approval is contingent on verifying clinical benefit (overall survival) in the confirmatory Phase 3 trial EV-301.
